overall_summary: Deduplication and recency weighting indicate that high-concept space phenomena—specifically extreme planetary environments, 'What If' hypothetical scenarios, and counterintuitive cosmic extremes—are significantly outperforming standard psychology, history, or basic animal trivia in velocity and engagement (likes-per-view). Videos featuring surreal planetary conditions (e.g., TrES-2b, liquid diamond planets, and burning ice worlds) consistently generate higher view velocities and strong engagement ratios within shorter timeframes.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) show high view counts and robust likes relative to their age.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on surreal planetary 'What If' scenarios that force the viewer to visualize extreme physical environments instantly.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible-sounding realities, such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0), are driving strong organic discovery.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks on absolute superlatives and counterintuitive planetary facts that challenge standard human intuition.

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic Psychological and Brain Trick Trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal psychological tricks or memory facts (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 5AN7LUgqarc) show stagnant or very low view velocities compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychology trivia unless paired with an extreme, high-stakes hypothetical scenario or a dramatic visual hook.
